1  THE RESPONDENT AND PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE PRL.
 JUDGE, FAMILY COURT AT BELAGAVI AND TRANSFER THE  SAME TO THE FAMILY COURT AT DAVANAGERE FOR DISPOSAL  IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE  AND EQUITY.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

This petition under Section 24 of CPC is filed by the petitioner-wife seeking for transfer of M.C.No.387/2023 pending on the file of the Principal Judge, Family Court, Belgavi to the Family Court in Davanagere.
2. The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of the respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 14.11.2019 in Davanagere as per Hindu rites and customs.
Out of the wedlock, the couple were blessed with a daughter, who is now aged about 3 years and she is in the custody of the petitioner.
After the marriage, the petitioner was residing with her husband at her matrimonial house in Belgavi.
In the year 2022, the matrimonial disputes arose between the parties, the petitioner started living separately with her parents in Davanagere.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed Crl.Misc.No.154/2023 before the Family Court, Davanagere for maintenance and she also lodged a complaint in Women Police Station, Davanagere in Crime NC: 2024:KHC:18215 No.119/2022 against her husband under Section 498A of IPC.
The same is also pending in the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Davanagere.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the respondent- husband filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act in M.C.No.387/2023 before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Belgavi for Restitution of Conjugal Right.

The case of the petitioner is that since the petitioner is residing in Davanagere, it would cause inconvenience and great hardship for her to travel a distance of 250 kms to Belgavi to prosecute the case.
Hence, she filed the present petition seeking for transfer of case.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner-wife contended that after the marriage, the petitioner was residing at her matrimonial house in Belgavi.
Out of thier wedlock, the couple have blessed with a daughter, who is now aged about 3 years and she is residing with her petitioner.
Thereafter, due to matrimonial disputes, the petitioner started living separately with her parents.

He further contended that the parents of the petitioner are aged NC: 2024:KHC:18215 persons and she has no other relatives or family members to assist her in traveling to Belgavi which is at a distance of 250 kms to prosecute the case.
Therefore, if the petition is not transferred, it would cause great inconvenience and hardship to the petitioner-wife.
Hence, he sought for allowing the petition.
4. The learned counsel for the respondent-husband contended that after the marriage, the petitioner was residing with her husband at Belgavi and she is familiar with the places in Belgavi.

Therefore,
she can travel from Davangere to Belgavi to prosecute the case.

Hence, he sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the petition papers.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner is the legally wedded wife of the respondent and their marriage marriage was solemnized on 14.11.2019 at as per Hindu rites and customs.
Out of their wedlock, the couple have been blessed with a girl child, who is now in the custody of the petitioner.
After the marriage, the petitioner was residing with her husband at her matrimonial house, Belgavi till 09.03.2022.
Thereafter, as matrimonial disputes arose between the parties, the petitioner along with her daughter started living separately with her parents in Davanagere.
The respondent-husband filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in M.C.No.387/2023 before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Belgavi for Restitution of Conjugal Right.

The case of the petitioner is that since the petitioner is residing in Davanagere and she has no other relatives or family members to assist her in traveling to Belgavi, it would cause inconvenience and great hardship for her to travel a distance of 250 kms from Davanagere to Belgavi to prosecute the case.

Insofar as the contention of the respondent that he faces threat from the family members of the petitioner when he attends the proceedings before the Court in Davanagere is concerned, he has not produced any document or police complaint filed against the petitioner or her family members about the threat.
If such being the case, the liberty is reserved to the respondent to file a police complaint against the petitioner or her family members before the jurisdictional police.

8. This Court in the case Smt.M.V.Rekha v. Sri Sathya @ Suraj - ILR 2010 KAR 5407 at Paragraph No.15 has held as hereunder:
"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that ends of justice demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

entities.text: Smt.M.V.Rekha v. Sri Sathya @ Suraj - ILR 2010 KAR 5407
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of either of the parties, the social strata of the spouses and behavioural NC:
2024:KHC:18215 pattern, their standard of life antecedent to marriage and subsequent thereon and the circumstances of either of the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
Generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.

Further, when two proceedings in different Courts which raise common question of fact and law and when the decisions are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions (See Smt.NandaKishori v. 9. Therefore, taking note of the inconvenience as made out by the petitioner and the law laid down in the case of Smt.M.V.Rekha (supra), which provides that convenience of the wife is an aspect that is to be taken note of while NC: 2024:KHC:18215 considering the transfer petitions, petition deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The petition is allowed.
b) The case in M.C.No.387/2023 pending on the file of the Principal Judge, Family Court, Belgavi is hereby withdrawn and the same is transferred to the Family Court in Davanagere.
c) The transferor Court is hereby directed to transmit the entire records to the transferee Court.
d) The transferee Court after hearing the parties is directed to dispose of the said case as expeditiously as possible and in accordance with law.
